# Development Android SDK Versions

# 

v8.8.0 - March 13, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed occasional app freezes that occurred when the SDK attempted to access local storage.
  * Fixed an issue in push campaign **Standard** and **Subscription** creatives where the app icon was displayed in place of the large icon if the SDK failed to retrieve the large icon image, for example, due to an invalid image URL. After this fix, no large icon is displayed if the SDK fails to retrieve the image.
  * Fixed rare crashes that occurred when the app was killed by the OS scheduler. Crashes occurred when receiving push notifications, and if the app crashed, the notification wouldn't be displayed by the device.



### 

Changed

  * Retail Media Network features have been deprecated.



* * *

# 

v8.7.2 - January 16, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed in-app campaign display failures on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Affected SDK versions: 8.5.0 to 8.7.1.
  * Fixed an issue where in-app campaigns failed to display and images were missing from push message campaigns on devices running Android 7.1 or earlier due to SSL handshake failures when connecting to certain image source URLs.



* * *

# 

v8.7.1 - January 2, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed a race condition causing display failures in push campaigns using the Banner creative. These campaigns still logged `notification_displayed` events even when they failed to display.
  * Fixed an issue preventing geofencing from functioning on certain device types running Android 16.



### 

Changed

  * If no large icon image is uploaded, the large icon will be omitted. Previously, if no large icon image was uploaded, the app icon was automatically used as a fallback.



### 

Known issues

  * In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v8.7.0 - December 18 , 2025

### 

New

  * Added support for [retrieving the Appier ID](doc:designing-creatives#capture-appier-ids-in-form-submissions) in Creative Studio lead generation campaigns.
  * Added support for switching between multiple app IDs. Contact your customer success manager to enable this feature.
  * Added support for edge-to-edge display for apps targeting Android 16.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue in the SDK's notification handling causing unexpected app crashes.
  * Fixed a memory leak in the SDK's notification handling.
  * Fixed a web view bridge issue causing the SDK's flushing method's (`appier('flushUserData', callback)`) callback method was executed before the flush operation completed.



### 

Known issues

  * In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v8.6.0 - October 23, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed failures in the in-app campaign trigger condition evaluation mechanism due to mismatched data types, causing in-app campaigns to fail to display. Now, data type normalization is applied before evaluating trigger conditions.
  * Fixed `GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_INTENTS` errors which occurred during geofence registration.
  * Fixed the incorrect logging of redundant `geofence_enter` and `geofence_exit` events.



### 

Changed

  * Deprecated Personalized Campaigns.



### 

Known issues

  * In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v8.5.1 - September 19, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Upgraded the Google Play Services Ads Identifier (`play-services-ads-identifier`) dependency from version 18.0.1 to 18.2.0 to address [CVE-2022-2390](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2022-2390) security vulnerability.



### 

Known issues

  * In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v8.5.0 - September 12, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Upgraded the SDK to target API level 35.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where the SDK version in `user_details` was logged after a delay of up to 12 hours if the app was launched by sending a push campaign after an app upgrade.



### 

Known issues

  * In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v8.4.1 - August 22, 2025

### 

New

  * Internal enhancements to improve CrossX ad performance.



* * *

# 

v8.4.0 - August 8, 2025

### 

New

  * Added real-time user event inferencing for recommendation scenarios, allowing results to reflect user behavior more quickly.
  * [`flush()`](doc:configuring-batching-for-android#force-flushing-stored-data) is now supported in web views.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed a crash that occurred when the SDK attempted to access Android location services which were unavailable.



* * *

# 

v8.3.2 - July 18, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Upgraded `socket.io-client` from version `1.0.2` to `2.1.2` to address [a known vulnerability](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/io.socket/socket.io-client/1.0.2). This dependency is only used for AiDeal features.



* * *

# 

v8.3.1 - June 20, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where calls to [`hideInApp()`](doc:in-app-popup-notifications-for-android#disabling-in-app-pop-up-notifications) failed if called before the SDK finished initializing. `hideInApp()` is now handled safely even if invoked during SDK initialization.
  * Fixed an issue where the key-value pairs of push campaigns using the **Subscription** creative included system data not specified in the campaign settings.
  * Fixed an issue causing [`fetchInboxMessages()`](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-android#fetchinboxmessages) to return no results for in-app inbox campaigns targeting the **New Users** default segment.
  * Fixed an issue causing geofence registration to fail when more than five geofences were registered. Geofencing is a beta feature. To learn more, contact your customer success manager.
  * Fixed a concurrency issue that could lead to a `ConcurrentModificationException` when processing campaign deep links.



### 

Changed

  * Updated ProGuard configurations to prevent compatibility issues with ProGuard rules for third-party SDKs.



* * *

# 

v8.3.0 - May 21, 2025

### 

New

  * Introduced new methods for handling key-value pairs sent via push notifications.



### 

Changed

  * In-app inbox campaigns returned by `getInboxes()` are now returned in campaign priority order. Previously, campaigns were returned in random order.



### 

Fixed

  * `fetchInboxMessages()` only fetches inbox campaigns on its first invocation—no inbox campaigns are fetched in subsequent calls. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.3.



* * *

# 

v8.2.5 - April 25, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Calling the `logEvent()` method occasionally caused unexpected app freezes and crashes.
  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is now correctly logged by the SDK. In versions 8.0.0 to 8.2.4, this event wasn't logged by the SDK.



* * *

# 

v8.2.4 - March 12, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Added logic to map incorrectly regenerated Appier IDs to their original correct IDs, enabling data recovery efforts initiated due to the known issue present in versions 8.2.0, 8.2.1, and 8.2.2.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.2.3 - March 11, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is no longer incorrectly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background). This issue is present in versions 8.2.0, 8.2.1, 8.2.2.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

#  v8.2.2 - February 24, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

Fixed

  * The following configuration APIs weren't successfully applied if they were called before the SDK finished initializating in SDK versions 8.0.0 to 8.2.1:
    * `QG.addJavaScriptInterface`
    * `QG.enablePushNotificationStorage`
    * `QG.setMaxNumStoredNotifications`
    * `QG.updateInboxRecordLimit`
    * `QG.setDataTrackingConfig`
  * Campaign creative changes for active in-app campaigns weren't applied after reopening the app from the background.



### 

Known issues

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is incorrectly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background) after upgrading to this SDK version. These regenerated Appier IDs were treated as new users, impacting related metrics and segments.
  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

#  v8.2.1 - February 7, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

Fixed

  * Apps unexpectedly crashed when users clicked on non-hierarchical URLs, such as `mailto:[[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)]`or `tel:+123456789`.



### 

Known issues

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is incorrectly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background) after upgrading to this SDK version. These regenerated Appier IDs were treated as new users, impacting related metrics and segments.
  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

#  v8.2.0 - January 17, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

Changed

  * Optimized data transmission process to the server.
  * Improved campaign stability to ensure that custom HTML campaigns remain active and uninterrupted when the campaign is expanded or collapsed, or when switching app pages.



### 

Fixed

  * The exit push notification was incorrectly sent again after the first exit push and the subsequent 10 push campaigns. Affected versions: v8.0.0 and later.
  * In-app campaigns failed to display when the system time was changed.



### 

Known issues

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is incorrectly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background) after upgrading to this SDK version. These regenerated Appier IDs were treated as new users, impacting related metrics and segments.
  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.1.0 - December 20, 2024

### 

New

  * Added app ID validation for app web views. If your app and website use different app IDs, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#d5b0a6a68aa6a0a5a5baa7a195b4a5a5bcb0a7fbb6bab8) ) to modify the SDK's app ID allowlist to ensure web data is logged to the correct app ID.



### 

Changed

  * Extracted the geofencing feature as a standalone library. For details about this beta feature, contact your customer success manager.
  * Removed the following SDK dependencies:
    * `com.google.android.gms:play-services-location:21.3.0`
    * `org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-play-services:1.4.1`
    * `com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.0.1`
  * The `model_id` parameter's data type (included in `recommendation_clicked` events) is now sent as a string. If you're logging this event, you'll need to modify your implementation. Please refer to [Android SDK: Recommendation 2.0](doc:android-sdk-recommendation-20#tracking-clicks-and-impressions) for details.



### 

Fixed

  * `qg_inapp_toggled` events are now correctly logged in the following scenarios:
    * Closing a HTML in-app campaign.
    * Clicking the action button of an in-app campaign with **Persist until the notification is clicked** is enabled.
  * Apps no longer experience occasional crashes due to an improperly configured `google-service.json` or using an incorrect sender ID.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.0.1 - November 15, 2024

### 

Fixed

  * In-app campaign floating icons no longer flicker due to unexpected rendering behavior.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.0.0 - October 31, 2024

### 

New

  * Support for Retail Media Network features (beta). To learn more, contact your customer success manager.
  * Support for AiDeal features (beta). To learn more, contact your customer success manager.



### 

Changed

  * [Banner creatives](doc:banner-image) are now fully expandable, displaying the title, message, and banner image simultaneously.
  * Updated to several [SDK dependencies](doc:resolving-dependency-conflicts#appier-android-sdk-dependencies).
    * Upgraded the `firebase-messaging` dependency from version `20.0.1` to `23.0.0`.
    * Removed the deprecated `firebase-iid` dependency.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.

# Stable Android SDK Versions

# 

v7.27.1 - January 16, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed in-app campaign display failures on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Affected SDK version: 7.27.0.



* * *

# 

v7.27.0 - September 26, 2025

### 

New

  * Edge-to-edge display support for apps targeting API level 35 or later.



### 

Changed

  * Deprecated Personalized Campaigns.



### 

Known issues

  * In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v7.26.0 - September 6, 2024

### 

New

  * Support interactions with background while an in-app creative studio campaign is displayed. Creative studio is a beta feature. To learn more, contact your customer success manager.



* * *

# 

v7.25.1 - August 30, 2024

### 

Fixed

  * Clicking the deep link in push campaigns where the deep link was set to an invalid URL caused the app to crash.
  * When push campaigns were stacked, clicking action buttons in any campaign redirected to the deep link configured in the most recently-received campaign.
  * Push notification small icons failed to display for apps using [adaptive icons](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/icon_design_adaptive).
  * On devices running Android 12+, clicking push notification action buttons missing deep links didn't launch the app.
  * In Carousel creatives, if a single carousel card was missing the headline and description, the headline and description failed to display for all cards in the carousel.
  * Slider creatives occasionally failed to display large images.
  * In-app pop-up campaign weren't dismissed and will reappeared if the blank margin is double-clicked quickly.
  * In-app pop-up campaigns experienced the following abnormal behavior when the device’s orientation was changed:

> 
>   * Campaign-level frequency cap does not work when the in-app campaign contains a deeplink. This issue has been fixed in Android SDK 7.0.1.
>   * In Android SDK 7.0.0, the `sdkVersion` is shown as 6.11.0.
>

# Android User Data Permission Controls

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Required SDK version
> 
> User data permissions controls are only available on Android SDK 7.23.0 or later.

## 

Overview

To allow your app to comply with data privacy policies and regulations, the Appier Android SDK allows you to manage user data permissions for the following types of data:

  * **Google Advertising ID (AAID)** : Collection is enabled by default.
  * **Location data** : Collection is disabled by default.



You can enable or disable collection for this data at any point in your app's lifecycle, even before the Appier SDK is initialized, and the changes will be effective immediately. For example, you may want to update user data collection settings in the following scenarios:

  * After the app is launched
  * After a user has responded to a data collection consent prompt
  * After [regenerating the user's Appier ID](managing-android-users#deleting-and-regenerating-android-users)
  * After a user logs in or logs out of their account



* * *

## 

AAID

### 

Retrieving the current user data collection settings

KotlinJava
    
    
    val collectAaid = QG.getInstance(context).dataTrackingConfig.collectAaid
    
    
    boolean collectAaid = QG.getInstance(context).dataTrackingConfig.getCollectAaid();

### 

Disabling AAID collection

AAID collection is enabled by default. To disable AAID collection, set `collectAaid` to `false`.

KotlinJava
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).dataTrackingConfig.collectAaid = false
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).dataTrackingConfig.setCollectAaid(false);

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> By default, the Appier SDK automatically collects the device's AAID upon initialization. If you want to avoid this scenario, we strongly recommend disabling AAID collection before initializing the Appier SDK.

* * *

## 

Location data

### 

Enabling location data collection

Location data collection is disabled by default. To enable location data collection, set `collectLocation` to `true`.

KotlinJava
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).dataTrackingConfig.collectLocation = true
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).getDataTrackingConfig().setCollectLocation(true);

* * *

## 

Sample data collection configuration

The following sample demonstrates how to configure data collection settings for multiple data types simultaneously:

KotlinJava
    
    
    val trackingConfig = DataTrackingConfig(collectLocation = false, collectAaid = false)
    trackingConfig.collectAaid = true   // The settings won't be applied since they're not assigned to QG.
    QG.getInstance(context).dataTrackingConfig = trackingConfig // The settings takes effect.
    
    
    DataTrackingConfig trackingConfig = new DataTrackingConfig(false, false);
    trackingConfig.setCollectAaid(true);  // The settings won't be applied since they're not assigned to QG.
    QG.getInstance(context).setDataTrackingConfig(trackingConfig); // The settings takes effect.

# App Tracking Transparency (iOS 14.5+)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> Support for App Tracking Transparency requires iOS SDK 7.9.0 or above.

Starting with iOS 14.5, Apple now requires app to ask for permission to track users using the device's advertising identifier (IDFA). See <https://developer.apple.com/app-store/user-privacy-and-data-use/>.

To do this, you will need to use the [App Tracking Transparency framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency) provided by Apple. Once the App Tracking Transparency framework is integrated, users will see a dialog box that asks for permission to track them.

![1000](https://files.readme.io/a2d44bb-Screen_Shot_2021-03-30_at_7.15.10_PM.png)

* * *

## 

Integrate the AppTrackingTransparency framework

Below is a brief summary on how to integrate the AppTrackingTransparency framework, but be sure to go through Apple's official documents on [AppTrackingTransparency framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency) for more details.

### 

Add usage description to `info.plist`

In your project’s `info.plist` file, add an `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription` key. Write a message describing the purpose for tracking user data that is specific to your use case. ​The message shown below is just an example.

Info.plist
    
    
    <key>NSUserTrackingUsageDescription</key>
    <string>This allows us to serve personalized contents and ads based on your browsing pattern across apps and websites.</string>

This message will be displayed on the dialog box to request user permission.

![1450](https://files.readme.io/80d326b-Screen_Shot_2021-05-06_at_6.48.47_PM.png)

### 

Request authorization to track

To request user's permission for tracking, add the AppTrackingTransparency framework to your app. Below is an example of requesting for user's permission at app launch.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import AppTrackingTransparency
    
    @available(iOS 14, *)
    func askATTPermission() {
        ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization { _ in
          ...
        }
    }
    
    
    #import <AppTrackingTransparency/ATTrackingManager.h>
    
    - (void)askATTPermission API_AVAILABLE(ios(14)) {
        [ATTrackingManager requestTrackingAuthorizationWithCompletionHandler:^(ATTrackingManagerAuthorizationStatus status) {
            ...
        }];
    }

If the user chooses to allow tracking, an `ATTrackingManagerAuthorizationStatusAuthorized` value will be returned. See [Apple's documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency/attrackingmanagerauthorizationstatus) for details on the authorization values available.

* * *

## 

Sending IDFA based on authorization status

If you want Appier SDK to collect IDFA only when an "Authorized" status is returned, call the `setIDFAConsent` method and set it to `true` for Swift or `YES` for Objective-C.

If `setIDFAConsent` is set to `false` or `NO`, Appier SDK will collect IDFA regardless of user's authorization status. However, depending on the user's authorization status, the IDFA collected may be valid or invalid (e.g. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). The same applies if `setIDFAConsent` is not set.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import Appier
    
    func sendingIDFAWhenAuthorized() {
        let qgsdk = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
        // If true, IDFA is sent ONLY if the user authorizes tracking
        // If false or not set, IDFA is sent regardless of user's authorization status
        qgsdk.setIDFAConsent(true)
    }
    
    
    #import <Appier/Appier.h>
    
    - (void)sendingIDFAWhenAuthorized {
        QGSdk *qgsdk = [QGSdk getSharedInstance];
        // If true, IDFA is sent ONLY if the user authorizes tracking
        // If false or not set, IDFA is sent regardless of user's authorization status
        [qgsdk setIDFAConsent:YES];
    }

# [iOS] App Tracking Transparency for React Native

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> **Note**
> 
> Note:
> 
> Support for App Tracking Transparency requires React Native SDK 1.5.0 or above.

Starting with iOS 14.5, Apple now requires app to ask for permission to track users using the device's advertising identifier (IDFA). See <https://developer.apple.com/app-store/user-privacy-and-data-use/>.

To do this, you will need to use the [App Tracking Transparency framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency) provided by Apple. Once the App Tracking Transparency framework is integrated, users will see a dialog box that asks for permission to track them.

![https://files.readme.io/a2d44bb-Screen_Shot_2021-03-30_at_7.15.10_PM.png](https://files.readme.io/a2d44bb-Screen_Shot_2021-03-30_at_7.15.10_PM.png)

* * *

  


## 

Integrate App Tracking Transparency Framework

Below is a brief summary on how to integrate App Tracking Transparency framework, but be sure to go through Apple's official documents on [AppTrackingTransparency framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency) for more details.

### 

Add Usage Description to Info.plist

In your project’s Info.plist file, add a `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription` key. Write a message describing the purpose for tracking user data that is specific to your use case. ​The message shown below is just an example.

Info.plist
    
    
    <key>NSUserTrackingUsageDescription</key>
    <string>This allows us to serve personalized contents and ads based on your browsing pattern across apps and websites.</string>

This message will be displayed on the dialog box to request user permission.

![https://files.readme.io/80d326b-Screen_Shot_2021-05-06_at_6.48.47_PM.png](https://files.readme.io/80d326b-Screen_Shot_2021-05-06_at_6.48.47_PM.png)

### 

Request Authorization to Track

To request user's permission for tracking, add the AppTrackingTransparency framework to your app. Below is an example of requesting for user's permission at app launch.

Swift
    
    
    import AppTrackingTransparency
    import Appier
    
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?) -> Bool {
    
        if #available(iOS 14, *) {
            ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization { _ in
                ...
            }
        }
    }

Objective-C
    
    
    #import <AppTrackingTransparency/ATTrackingManager.h>
    
    #import <Appier/Appier.h>
    
    - (BOOL)application:(UIApplication *)application didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:(NSDictionary *)launchOptions {
    
        if (@available(iOS 14.0, *)) {
            [ATTrackingManager requestTrackingAuthorizationWithCompletionHandler:^(ATTrackingManagerAuthorizationStatus status) {
                ...
            }];
        }
    }

If the user chooses to allow tracking, an `ATTrackingManagerAuthorizationStatusAuthorized` value will be returned. See [Apple's documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency/attrackingmanagerauthorizationstatus) for details on the authorization values available.

* * *

  


## 

Sending IDFA Based on Authorization Status

If you want Appier SDK to collect IDFA only when an "Authorized" status is returned, call the `setIDFAConsent` method and set it to `true` in your react-native application.

If `setIDFAConsent` is set to `false`, Appier SDK will collect IDFA regardless of user's authorization status. However, depending on the user's authorization status, the IDFA collected may be valid or invalid (e.g. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). The same applies if `setIDFAConsent` is not set.

Put the code snippet below into your initilization method.

JavaScript
    
    
    RNAiqua.configure({
      appId: '<your appId>',
      appGroup: '<iOS App Group>',
      isDev: true // ios dev or prod - default is true
    });
    //If true, IDFA is sent ONLY if user authorizes tracking
    //If false or not set, IDFA is sent regardless of user's authorization status
    RNAiqua.setIDFAConsent(true);

# Apple App Privacy

## 

Overview

Starting from December 2020, Apple requires developers to disclose the privacy practices of the app: <https://developer.apple.com/app-store/app-privacy-details/>.

When submitting your app to the App Store, you'll need to answer a series of questions about the data collected by you and your third-party partners, includes the data collected by the Appier iOS SDK. Refer to the data collection and usage table for a list of all the data collected by the Appier iOS SDK.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> You may need to provide additional disclosures based on your app's data collection practices and any other third-party partners you are using.

### 

App privacy manifest (iOS SDK 7.32.0 or later)

Starting from iOS SDK 7.32.0, the Appier SDK provides a privacy manifests which allows you to automatically generate an [App Privacy Report](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/privacy_manifest_files/describing_data_use_in_privacy_manifests#4239187). The App Privacy Report summarizes the data collected and used by your app, including the third-party SDKs your app uses.

  * The Appier SDK's privacy manifest only includes the required data (✅) as listed in the data collection and usage table.
  * For optional data (▵), you should complete Apple's Privacy Nutrition Labels based on your app's specific usage requirements.



* * *

## 

Data Collection

Under "General > App Privacy" in App Store Connect, click **Get Started** and select **Yes, we collect data from this app**.

![](https://files.readme.io/a1b0446-Screenshot_2020-12-17_at_18.22.46.png)

### 

Part I: Select the Data Types Collected

You'll see a list of data types, and you'll need to select the types of data collected from your app. **Refer to the Part I column** in the table below for the data collected by Appier iOS SDK.

![](https://files.readme.io/a8a6eb6-Screenshot_2020-12-17_at_18.26.37.png)

### 

Part II: Select How Each Data Type is Used

For each data type you select, you'll need to select from the list below to indicate how the data is being used in your app. **Refer to the Part II column** in the data collection and usage table below for how the data is used by Appier iOS SDK.

![](https://files.readme.io/fdb210a-Screenshot_2020-12-18_at_11.56.26.png)

### 

Part III: Answer Yes/No Questions

Next, you will have to answer some Yes/No questions such as:

  * Are the <Data Type> collected from this app linked to the user's identity?
  * Do you or your third-party partners use <Data Type> for tracking purposes?



**Refer to the Part III column** in the data collection and usage table below for how the data is used by Appier iOS SDK.

* * *

## 

Data collection and usage

✅ = Always required when using the Appier iOS SDK  
▵ = May be required when using the Appier iOS SDK  
❌ = Not required when using the Appier iOS SDK

Part I: What Data Is Collected| Part II: How Is It Used?| Part III: Yes/No Questions  
---|---|---  
**[Contact Info]** ▵ Name ▵ Email Address ▵ Phone Number ▵ Physical Address ▵ Other User Contact Info(▵ = Select if you collect these data via Appier iOS SDK)| ✅ Developer's Advertising or Marketing  
✅ Analytics  
▵ Product Personalization(▵ = Select if you are using Recommendation or Personalization features)| • Linked to the user's identity? **YES** ✅  
• Tracking purposes? **YES** ✅  
❌ **[Health and Fitness]**| |   
❌ **[Financial Info]**| |   
**[Location]**  
▵ Precise Location  
▵ Coarse Location(▵ = Select if you enabled location collection)| ✅ Analytics| • Linked to the user's identity? **YES** ✅  
• Tracking purposes? **YES** ✅  
❌ **[Sensitive Info]**| |   
❌ **[Contacts]**| |   
❌ **[User Content]**| |   
❌ **[Browsing History]**| |   
❌ **[Search History]**| |   
**[Identifiers]**  
✅ User ID  
✅ Device ID| ✅ Developer's Advertising or Marketing  
✅ Analytics  
▵ Product Personalization(▵ = Select if you are using Recommendation or Personalization features)| • Linked to the user's identity? **YES** ✅  
• Tracking purposes? **YES** ✅  
▵ **[Purchases]**(▵ = Select if you collect purchase-related events via Appier iOS SDK)| ✅ Developer's Advertising or Marketing  
✅ Analytics  
▵ Product Personalization(▵ = Select if you are using Recommendation or Personalization features)| • Linked to the user's identity? **YES** ✅  
• Tracking purposes? **YES** ✅  
**[Usage Data]**  
✅ Product Interaction  
❌ Advertising Data  
❌ Other Usage Data| ✅ Developer's Advertising or Marketing  
✅ Analytics  
▵ Product Personalization(▵ = Select if you are using Recommendation or Personalization features)| • Linked to the user's identity? **YES** ✅  
• Tracking purposes? **YES** ✅  
**[Diagnostics]**  
✅ Crash Data  
❌ Performance Data  
❌ Other Diagnostic Data| ✅ App Functionality| • Linked to the user's identity? **YES** ✅  
• Tracking purposes? **NO** ❌  
❌ **[Other Data]**| |   
  
After you are done, you will see a preview of your app's privacy practices that will be shown to users in the app store.

# AppsFlyer Integration Guide

## 

Overview

Integrating AppsFlyer with AIQUA offers significant benefits for enhancing marketing strategies and outcomes. AppsFlyer provides robust measurement, analytics, and fraud protection, ensuring accurate attribution and performance metrics across multiple channels and devices. By combining these capabilities with AIQUA's omnichannel marketing automation features, you can create targeted campaigns, optimize customer journeys, and increase conversions.

Before proceeding with the AppsFlyer integration, ensure you've completed the integration prerequisites. Once the prerequisites have been completed, follow these steps to complete the AppsFlyer integration with your app.

  1. Initialize the AppsFlyer SDK and track data.
  2. Add the Appier integration to your AppsFlyer app.
  3. Verify that events are collected properly.



### 

Prerequisites

Ensure you've met the following prerequisites before continuing with this guide:

  * Retrieve your AppsFlyer dev key (**Settings > App Settings > SDK authentication**).

  * Integrate your app with the Appier iOS or Android SDK. For detailed instructions, see these guides:

    * [iOS SDK Overview](doc:ios-sdk-integration-overview)
    * [Android SDK Overview](doc:android-sdk-overview)
  * Provide your app’s ID to your customer success manager. The app ID can be found in the app's URL. Refer to the instructions below for Android and iOS.




#### 

Retrieving your Android app ID

Retrieve the Android app ID from the `id` query parameter.

Example app URL| Example app ID  
---|---  
`https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox&hl=en`| `com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox`  
  
#### 

Retrieving your iOS app ID.

Retrieve the iOS app ID from the final portion of the URL, only including the portion after `id`.

Example app URL| Example app ID  
---|---  
`https://apps.apple.com/us/app/google/id284815942`| `284815942`  
  
* * *

## 

1\. Initialize the AppsFlyer SDK and track data

Follow the steps corresponding to the platform your app is for:

  * iOS
  * Android



#### 

iOS

  1. Initialize the AppsFlyer SDK.



Swift
    
    
    AppsFlyerLib.shared().appsFlyerDevKey = "<YOUR_APPSFLYER_DEV_KEY>"
    AppsFlyerLib.shared().appleAppID = "<YOUR_APPLE_APP_ID>"

  2. Before tracking data:
     1. Initialize the Appier SDK.
     2. Use the AppsFlyer SDK to assign values for the following custom data fields: `appier_app_id` and `appier_user_id`.



Swift
    
    
    let sdk = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
    sdk.onStart("<YOUR_APPIER_APP_ID>", setDevProfile: false)
    let appierAppId = "<YOUR_APPIER_APP_ID>"
    let appierUserId = sdk.getAppierId()
    
    AppsFlyerLib.shared().customData = ["appier_app_id": appierAppId, "appier_user_id": appierUserId]

  3. Start tracking data with the AppsFlyer SDK.



Swift
    
    
    AppsFlyerLib.shared().start()

#### 

Android

  1. Initialize the AppsFlyer SDK.



Java
    
    
    AppsFlyerLib.getInstance().init("<YOUR_APPSFLYER_DEV_KEY>", null, application);

  2. Before tracking data:
     1. Initialize the Appier SDK.
     2. Use the AppsFlyer SDK to assign values for the following custom data fields: `appier_app_id` and `appier_user_id`.



Java
    
    
    QG.initializeSdk(application, "<YOUR_APPIER_APP_ID>");
    String appierAppId = "<YOUR_APPIER_APP_ID>";
    String appierUserId = QG.getInstance(application).getAppierId();
    
    Map<String, Object> customData = new HashMap<>();
    customData.put("appier_app_id", appierAppId);
    customData.put("appier_user_id", appierUserId);
    
    AppsFlyerLib.getInstance().setAdditionalData(customData);

  3. Start tracking data with the AppsFlyer SDK.



Java
    
    
    AppsFlyerLib.getInstance().start(application);

* * *

## 

2\. Add the Appier integration to your AppsFlyer app

  1. Log in to the AppsFlyer console and go to **Collaborate > Partner Marketplace**

![](https://files.readme.io/ed219f2f485104edf3fdd2133a7738b496981616f1813c35efc9f97b816ee83b-appsflyer-partner-marketplace.png)

  2. Search for "Appier", select the **Appier** integration, and click **Set up integration** to open the integration settings page.

![](https://files.readme.io/dfc7915ac23d26fabc4c0d13cf306a55277c15f38ab19708ba198518279a84fa-appesflyer-set-up-integration.png)

  3. Toggle **Activate partner**.

![](https://files.readme.io/03c5beac566fa9a967af407ae8e90b1d0a95cd674d6576e402119332c0987192-appsflyer-activate-partner.png)

  4. Enable **In-app event postbacks** , set the event postback window, and choose the events to send to Appier.

![](https://files.readme.io/bbc52d4afc36e2be458b8fbbc9985373e19d8497e56d1b212eba627685bf9e7c-appsflyer-in-app-event-postback.png)

  5. Click **Save Integration**.

![](https://files.readme.io/432269e50cb870b882d91ca4bd89461ad96d643109918687a8574326d59a668d-appsflyer-save-integration.png)

* * *

## 

3\. Verify that events are collected properly

  1. On the AppsFlyer console, go to **Analyze > Events** to see if events are being collected.

![](https://files.readme.io/c3e2a2654811082bdecb43e8e89455f3df6b22f25059ad7cae4f075d18a17428-appsflyer-console-events.png)

  2. On the AIQUA dashboard, click your email in the bottom left corner and go to **Recent activity**. Select the platform your app is on to verify that app events are displaying as expected.

![](https://files.readme.io/ff495b18aafcc39ad2d3d1dfc5eb3fd65936f5a50fc12ff5db4b2be2a09eda86-appsflyer-events.png)

# Why are users receiving delayed notifications?

Due to external factors, it's possible for users to receive delayed notifications, potentially leading to issues such as receiving notifications during a blackout window. Possible reasons for delayed notifications include:

  * Misconfigured device network settings (for example, DNS or VPN settings).
  * The mobile device can't receive the notification when it is initially sent (for example, if the device is offline or powered off).

# Content Assistant

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Beta feature
> 
> Content assistant is a beta feature. While this feature is currently available for use, you may encounter occasional bugs or stability issues.

AIQUA's campaign content assistant leverages generative AI to automatically create written content for your campaign creatives.

  * Automatically generate multiple marketing messages in seconds.
  * Reduce or entirely eliminate manual effort required to create marketing content for A/B testing.
  * Instantly get inspiration and ideas for marketing copy.



Content assistant is supported for the following types of regular push campaigns:

  * [Push](doc:campaigns-regular-create-push) (Android, iOS, and web)
  * [Instant messaging](doc:campaigns-regular-create-instant-messaging) (LINE, Kakao)

![](https://files.readme.io/90e1c15b0327cc42cb7078f33884a4facee193e2f9b367d210df7e5a48844563-open-content-assistant.png)

* * *

## 

How to use content assistant

### 

1\. Open content assistant

To open content assistant, open the campaign's creation page, go to the **Creative** section, then click **Content assistant**.

![](https://files.readme.io/3396c8a5e2bffad1a77ce397fc795c803430577de323f5801dcd193dc404296a-content-assistant.png)

### 

2\. Enter a description for your campaign

In the **Describe your campaign** field, enter one of the following:

  * A content generation prompt (keywords, descriptions, marketing scenarios).
  * Content that you want to modify, for example, content that must be shortened to fit a target length, or modified to match a certain tone.

![](https://files.readme.io/29bfd47-small-content-assistant-prompt.png)

### 

3\. Set the length, language, and tone for generated content

Next, set the settings for content length, language, and tone that best suit your campaign:

Setting| Description  
---|---  
**Target message length**|  The number of characters in the generated content.   
• Includes content for all applicable fields, for example, the combined length of the generated **Title** , **Subtitle** , and **Message**.   
• Maximum length is 500 characters.  
**Language**|  The desired language of the generated content.  
**Tone**|  The conversational style that the generated content should be written in.  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/92a0eba-small-content-assistant-additional-settings.png)

### 

4\. Generate and apply the content to your campaign

Once you've selected the desired settings, click **Generate content** , and three options for suggested content will be generated.

  * To browse between the three options, click the arrows on either side of the suggested content.
  * Once you've decided on the option you want to use, click **Apply suggestion** to automatically populate the campaign settings with the content suggestion.

![](https://files.readme.io/cb25247-small-content-assistant-apply-suggestion.png)

If none of the options are satisfactory, click **Regenerate** to generate a brand new set of suggestions, or click **Edit settings** to modify your content settings before regenerating new suggestions.

![](https://files.readme.io/4cfa857-small-content-assistant-edit-settings-regenerate.png)

# Experiments

Experiments allow you to create different variations of a creative and test what works best for your audience. For example, you can use a different image in each variant to see which creative performs the best.

### 

Supported campaign types

This feature is supported in the following campaign types.

Supported campaign types| Docs| Notes  
---|---|---  
In-web campaigns:   
All except subscription boost| See [here](doc:campaigns-experiments-in-web-and-in-app)| \--  
In-app campaigns: Pop-up| See [here](doc:campaigns-experiments-in-web-and-in-app)| Control groups are supported in the following Appier SDK versions:   
• iOS SDK 7.6.0 or later   
• Android SDK 6.8.0 or later  
Message campaigns| See [here](doc:campaigns-experiments-message)| Control groups are not supported.  
  
### 

Best practices

  * Test one variable at a time to pinpoint what's affecting the outcome.
  * To make sure the results are statistically significant, include enough users in each group and allow enough performance data to accumulate.
  * For in-app and in-web campaigns, do not run more than one experiment with the same trigger rule at the same time.
  * After creating an experiment campaign, you can use that campaign's notification IDs to create segmentation conditions, allowing you to target specific users based on their interaction with the campaign. To learn more, see [How do I segment by notification ID](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/how-do-i-segment-by-notification-id).

# Experiments: In-Web and In-App Campaigns

Use the experiment feature to test different variations of a creative and determine what works best for your audience. For example, you can use different call-to-action messages or creative types in each variant to see which one drives more conversions.

* * *

## 

Limitations

  * Experiments are supported for all in-web campaigns, except those designed with the [Subscription boost](doc:creatives-in-web-basic-templates-subscription-boost) template.
  * Once an experiment campaign starts running, it can no longer be edited.
  * Once an experiment campaign is stopped, it can't be restarted.



* * *

## 

Create an experiment

You can add experiments when creating an [in-web campaign](doc:campaigns-in-web-create) or [in-app campaign](doc:campaigns-in-app-create).

To start an experiment, click **\+ Add variant** and adjust **Traffic allocation** of each variant, or click **Divide equally**. The percentage must add up to 100% for all variants.

![](https://files.readme.io/8d780631c2a38e772db286d7c07258f7dcdfaf271e2b4dbbf96ed27d6d9c5910-experiments-variants.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> An experiment campaign can't be edited after it starts running, verify your configuration before publishing the campaign.

* * *

## 

View campaign performance

To view results, go to the campaign list, click on the campaign's name to open its performance page. For details about performance page, metrics, and definitions, see:

[ ![In-web campaigns](https://files.readme.io/bcb6b533f4a83a6ff9ca8a3688cb761b3acf94f199a2ef6b6b9037f5b48056f9-In-web_Campaign.png) In-web campaigns ](/docs/performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance#in-web-campaigns) [ ![In-app campaigns](https://files.readme.io/d0b5fb685e7b50c1594ae5a242f4b580133a8dbd8186300d5f08cb6f9b75bbcf-In-app_Campaign.png) In-app campaigns ](/docs/performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance#in-app-campaigns)

  


> 📘
> 
> In the campaign list, the numbers only include the performance of all variants. The performance of the control group is not included.
>
